where: blaze: a build script that reads the clock and runs git (reth-node-core, vergen)
what: In every edit's build of reth the span `build script run reth-node-core` took 14.7 s (its process lived 1.4 s): its kept run is looked up by hashing the 2,916 files and 590 listings of the checkout it read through `git status`, the edited file is one of them, so it ran again, and its new build time stamp made its crate and the six above it again (14 units a leaf body edit against 8).
cost: 13 to 15 s and 6 units of every edit; reth's own source says debug builds must not run it again
cause: cargo's rule was added to the trace of an untraceable run, never put in its place
whys: why slow: 2,916 files hashed, a script run, 6 units
why: the run's key holds everything it read
why: blaze keys a run by its trace
why wrong here: the run read the clock, so it is no function of its trace, and the script said what reruns it
property: exactness of inputs claimed for a run that has none
class: a key that is exact about inputs a value does not depend on functionally: cost with no correctness bought
prevention: built (4787b9a562, decision reth-1112-D2): an untraceable run whose script said its reruns is kept by cargo's rule and its own package's reads; invariant and control in blaze-usercode/src/rule.rs. Not built: a traceable run's checkout reads valued from the view instead of hashed from the disk
